case_name: Donald Ecret and Kristen Ecret v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: Wife, a former registered nurse disabled in 2014, received about $42,000/yr New York workers' compensation and SSDI subject to workers' compensation offset (42 U.S.C. §424a).

adjustments: increased base of Social Security benefits by $49,128 ($1,080 withholding + $48,048 workers' compensation offset) under sec. 86(d)(3)
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Taxability of Social Security benefits not paid in cash because of workers' compensation offset
conceded: Petitioners conceded unreported taxable interest of $33 and dividends of $38
Respondent conceded Social Security benefits treated as received in 2019 are only $19,866 (not $55,248); retroactive benefits attributable to 2016-2018 not taxed in 2019

findings_of_fact.fact: Wife received approximately $42,000 of New York workers' compensation annually 2014-2019
findings_of_fact.snippet: approximately $42,000 of such benefits annually through 2019, the tax year at issue.

findings_of_fact.fact: SSA: effective January 2018 ACE $5,074; 80% of ACE $4,059 per month; annual cap $48,708
findings_of_fact.snippet: 80% of her monthly ACE was $4,059. On an annual basis,

findings_of_fact.fact: 2019 Form SSA-1099: total benefits $55,248, of which $19,866 attributable to 2019 and $35,382 retroactive to 2016-2018
findings_of_fact.snippet: It indicated that she had total Social Security benefits of $55,248, of which $19,866 was attributable to 2019.

findings_of_fact.fact: 2019: $6,120 paid in cash, $1,080 voluntary withholding, $48,048 not paid due to workers' compensation offset
findings_of_fact.snippet: The balance of the $55,248 in benefits, or $48,048, was not paid on account of the “workers’ compensation offset.”

findings_of_fact.fact: Of 2019-attributable benefits, $12,666 was offset by workers' compensation ($6,120 + $1,080 + $12,666 = $19,866)
findings_of_fact.snippet: The SSA did not disburse the remaining $12,666 on account of the workers’ compensation offset .

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioners reported $5,202 taxable Social Security (85% of $6,120); 85% inclusion ratio applies (not disputed)
findings_of_fact.snippet: They appear to have calculated this sum as 85% of the $6,120 cash payment from the SSA.

issues.question: Under sec. 86(d)(3), is petitioner wife treated as receiving $19,866 of Social Security benefits in 2019 (including $12,666 offset by workers' compensation), and what amount is taxable?
issues.holding: Yes; benefits of $19,866 include the $12,666 workers' compensation offset; 85% inclusion gives taxable benefits of $16,886; petitioners must include an additional $11,684 ($16,886 - $5,202)
issues.computable_reason: Sec. 86(d)(3) adds offset amount to benefits; 85% of $19,866 = $16,886 less $5,202 reported

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: Taxable Social Security benefits for 2019 are $16,886 (additional $11,684); respondent conceded retroactive portion and penalty; petitioners conceded $33 interest and $38 dividends

notes: Legal question; facts undisputed. 85% inclusion ratio applied by agreement (other income not detailed). 2018 year dismissed for lack of jurisdiction: petition filed Feb. 22, 2022 was 108 days late for the Aug. 9, 2021 notice (fn. 4). Court rounds to nearest dollar. Derived: 0.85 x 19,866 = 16,886.1.
